records.shared_stimulus: A ball is dropped from rest in ideal free fall. Use g ≈ 10 m/s² and d = ½gt².
parts: (a) Predict the speed gained after 2 s.
(b) Calculate the distance fallen after 2 s.

(d) Explain which conclusions would need revision if air resistance became significant.

A ball is dropped from rest in ideal free fall. Use g ≈ 10 m/s² and d = ½gt².

  1. Predict the speed gained after 2 s.

records.primary_i_can: I can explain why objects in free fall accelerate at the same rate when air resistance is ignored.
records.evidence_job: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_action: Use the scenario evidence to make a physics claim and explain why it is consistent with the target.
records.intended_reasoning: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_text: Two compact objects of different masses are released together in a vacuum chamber near Earth. Predict which reaches the floor first and explain using the meaning of free fall.
records.student_html: Two compact objects of different masses are released together in a vacuum chamber near Earth. Predict which reaches the floor first and explain using the meaning of free fall.
records.answer: They reach the floor together if released from the same height with the same initial velocity. With air resistance ignored, both have the same downward acceleration g.
records.solution_text: In ideal free fall, gravity is the only significant force and all objects near Earth share the same gravitational acceleration regardless of mass.
records.solution_html: In ideal free fall, gravity is the only significant force and all objects near Earth share the same gravitational acceleration regardless of mass.

records.primary_i_can: I can use g ≈ 10 m/s² to determine speed gained during free fall.
records.evidence_job: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_action: Identify the relevant values, apply the appropriate relationship, report units, and interpret the result in context.
records.intended_reasoning: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_text: Ignoring air resistance, an object is dropped from rest. Using g ≈ 10 m/s², determine the speed it has gained after 3 s.
records.student_html: Ignoring air resistance, an object is dropped from rest. Using g ≈ 10 m/s², determine the speed it has gained after 3 s.
records.solution_text: Speed gained = g t = (10 m/s²)(3 s) = 30 m/s. Direction is downward.
records.solution_html: Speed gained = g t = (10 m/s²)(3 s) = 30 m/s. Direction is downward.

records.primary_i_can: I can use free-fall patterns to compare distance fallen during different time intervals and distinguish free fall from falling with significant air resistance.
records.evidence_job: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_action: Identify the relevant values, apply the appropriate relationship, report units, and interpret the result in context.
records.intended_reasoning: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_text: For ideal free fall from rest, use d = ½gt² with g ≈ 10 m/s². Compare the total distance fallen after 3 s and 4 s. Then explain why a coffee filter falling at terminal speed would not follow this same pattern.
records.student_html: For ideal free fall from rest, use d = ½gt² with g ≈ 10 m/s². Compare the total distance fallen after 3 s and 4 s. Then explain why a coffee filter falling at terminal speed would not follow this same pattern.
records.answer: After 3 s: 45 m; after 4 s: 80 m. The ideal distance grows with t². A filter with significant air resistance is not in ideal free fall and can reach nearly constant speed.
records.solution_text: d=5t² gives 45 m and 80 m. Significant air resistance changes the acceleration, so the ideal free-fall model no longer applies.
records.solution_html: d=5t² gives 45 m and 80 m. Significant air resistance changes the acceleration, so the ideal free-fall model no longer applies.
